zones.label: Column 1

Used only as a secondary identification aid, not as a diplomatic transcription. https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

lines.note: Continues Ame ic- from f258: rain fell as though poured out, with an extraordinary intensity. The scan shows no full stop after furite; vobitataxicari- continues below.

Qeri completes the past narrative form. Fox. is a citation label followed by book 2; the Portuguese describes rain falling in torrents. The contiguous era corrects OCR er a, while printed acantaros remains joined.
The rain was astonishing and extraordinary. The printed extra ordinaria is kept as two words, completing the translation rather than a new entry.
Ikkoku is a short unit or interval of time, paraphrased hitotsu no toki. The initial I and the damaged tç sequence are recovered from the scan, not OCR l and tg.
The second gloss is a brief span of time. Eſpaço is retained; no modern conversion into minutes is imposed on the dictionary's explanation.

The headword concerns double speech and refers back to iccô on f258. Its mixed caron/circumflex sequence is preserved, as is the different sequence in the divided example; these are not regularized to one spelling. The cross-reference iccô is embedded in Latin prose.

runs.text: Homem que falla por duas bo-

lines.note: Jetna fito completes the adjectival example, describing a person who speaks as though with two mouths. Bo- continues into bocas below.

runs.text: cas. i, que tendo hũa ſoo boca falla couſas

lines.note: Cas completes bocas, immediately explained as one actual mouth speaking incompatible things. The Portuguese clarification rules out a literal anatomical interpretation.
Diſcrepantes completes the characterization of inconsistent or contradictory speech. The short row closes the example before the market entry.
Ichi is a market or fair. Ichi ga tatsu means that a market is held; the printed example joins Ichigatatçu, and fei- continues below.
Ra completes feira. Ichi ni tatsu is glossed as going to market; Per begins a figurative-use marker continued as met. on the next row.
Kisen ichi wo nasu figuratively brings people of high and low station together. The Portuguese Ajuntaremſe continues with todos on the next row; its punctuation is retained as printed.

The gloss specifies everyone, high and low. The next example is monzen ni ichi wo nasu; the severely faded vowel after j is read e from the surviving compatible trace and phrase context, rather than OCR o. The elevated final i belongs to ichi, not a full stop.
Wo nasu completes the example of a crowd at the gate. The Portuguese mentions many people and horses; caua- is divided across the row boundary.
Los completes caualos. A further figurative use is prosperity in honours and receiving visitors, introduced by the printed Permet. marker.

runs.text: em honras, ſer viſitado de muitos, &c.

lines.note: The person prospers in honours and is visited by many. This completes the figurative extension of the market image, not an additional standalone headword.
Ichiba is the place where a market is held. The gloss defines the marketplace rather than another name for the fair itself.
Ichibetsu denotes a parting or separation. Apartamento is understood in that historical sense, not as a modern dwelling; the checked final t remains unexpanded.
Ichiboku is one low-ranking servant, paraphrased hitori no shimobe. The abbreviated Hũ and printed baixo are retained without adding omitted nasal letters.
Ichikatsu is a rebuke or reprimand. Bup. marks Buddhist usage and remains an upright printed label, not part of the Japanese headword.
Ichidan is an intensifying adverb, with hitokire as its Japanese paraphrase. The initial is capital I; gran continues into grandemente without a supplied hyphen.

runs.text: ſerue pera louuar, abaixar, ou abater.

lines.note: Demente completes grandemente. The explanation says the intensifier serves for praise as well as lowering or disparaging; the scan has abater, not OCR abuter.
This ichidan means one discourse or conversation, paraphrased hitotsu kataru. It is distinct from the preceding intensifying adverb despite the shared spelling.
Ichidoo is one hall or chapel, paraphrased hitotsu no doo. The damaged tç in Fitotçuno is restored; both printed long-o marks are carons.
Pella completes capella and the comparison with a church. The Portuguese explains the religious building without identifying it with a particular modern institution.
This ichidoo is one way or discipline, interpreted as an art. The final upright I- begins the divided example Ichidǒno taxxa; it is not a lowercase l or an italic dash.
I- plus chidǒno taxxa describes someone accomplished in one discipline. The Portuguese calls him outstanding in an art; Homẽ carries a faint nasal abbreviation and is separated from inſigne.
Ichidoo here means together or in the same manner, paraphrased hitotsu onaji. Its circumflex is distinguished from the carons in the preceding entries.
Meſma maneira completes the second gloss, 'in the same way'. This belongs to the collective or uniform sense of ichidoo.
Ichihatsu is one bowlful or portion, with hitotsu no hachi as its Japanese paraphrase. The Portuguese continues by naming a rice bowl.
A Goqui of rice specifies the portion. Goqui is a Japanese vessel term embedded in Portuguese prose, so it is recorded for whole-word typeface review rather than treated as a new headword.
This homographic ichihatsu is one hair, glossed hum cabello. The double l is preserved and no vowel is appended to the checked final t of the Japanese.
Ichiga is one and the same river, hitotsu no kawa. The terminal mark is a colon, not OCR's hyphen; it introduces the restriction on use below.

runs.text: mas não ſe vſa ſe não em compoſição de outras

lines.note: The dictionary says ichiga is used only in combination with other words. The two negatives frame that restriction, and the historical vſa spelling is preserved.
The example is ichiga no nagare wo kumu, drawing water from the same river. The final cu- is continued on the following physical line.

runs.text: Tirar, ou tomar agoa da corrente do

lines.note: Mu completes kumu. The Portuguese translates drawing or taking water from the current of the same river, whose final identification follows below.
Meſmo rio completes the translation. This short continuation closes the river entry without being merged into the following headword.
Ichigai concerns acting according to one's own will. Ichi- begins the example ichigai wo tatsuru; the Portuguese sense here is obstinacy, not a modern categorical adverb.
The example means insisting on one's own will. The right-edge mark divides pertinaz-mente rather than closing the sentence; the nasal abbreviation in võtade is retained.
Mente completes the manner adverb, 'obstinately'. Ichigaina mono begins the next example, describing an obstinate person.
Pertinaz completes homem pertinaz, the translation of ichigaina mono. It is the adjective's gloss, not a new lemma.
Ichigan is one eye, paraphrased hitotsu manako. The visible initial is capital I rather than the OCR's lowercase i.

runs.text: Hũa oração, ou compoſição de pala-

lines.note: Ichige is a verbal composition whose sense is not complete on its own. The scan supplies the missing i in the headword and joins oração; pala- continues below.

runs.text: uras que não tem ſentença perfeita.

lines.note: Uras completes palauras. The clause says the composition does not form a complete sense or statement; it should not be modernized into a different grammatical definition.
This ichige is one summer, paraphrased hito natsu and glossed verão or eſtio. The lowercase initial is retained from the aligned text and visible small type.
Ichigei is one art or skill, hitotsu no gei. The headword's vowel is i, matching the clearly printed example below, rather than OCR Ichuguei.
Ichigei no aru hito describes a person possessing an outstanding skill. The Portuguese ends with the faint full word eminente, not a divided eminent-; the next row begins em.
The person is eminent in some art. The initial is em, not OCR om; algua is retained without adding a tilde that is not secure in this impression.
Ichigen is one word or utterance, hitotsu no kotoba. The scan supports palaura, not OCR paliura; the example explains judging a speaker from an utterance.
Hito wa sono ichigen wo kiite begins the maxim: hearing a person's word reveals wisdom or folly. The damaged o in Fitoua and complete Vt are restored; qengu continues with its object particle below.
Wo shiru mono nari concludes the Japanese assertion. The Portuguese begins 'men, hearing', and continues with the content of what is heard.

runs.text: hũa palaura a alguẽ ſabem ſe tẽ ſaber, ou naõ.

lines.note: Hearing one word from someone, people know whether that person has understanding. The nasal abbreviations and printed naõ are retained without regularizing the tilde placement.
This ichigen is one source or origin, hitotsu no minamoto. The initial of Fitotçuno is F, not OCR I; prin- continues into principio.
Cipio completes principio, the Portuguese 'beginning' or 'principle'. It closes the origin entry, distinct from the preceding word or utterance sense.
Ichigi is one matter, paraphrased hitotsu no gi. The scan has c in Ichigui and a capital F in Fitotçuno, correcting two recognition errors.
Ichigyoo is one act or practice, hitotsu no okonai. The gloss offers an act or virtue, with the latter on the next row; the printed long-o mark is a caron.
Virtude completes the alternative gloss for the act or practice. This short line does not introduce a separate Japanese lemma.
This ichigyoo is one deed or work, hitotsu no waza. Its circumflex is retained rather than harmonized with the preceding caroned headword.
Ichigyuu denotes one bovine, paraphrased ushi ippiki and glossed as a cow or buffalo. The caron over u is preserved as the visible mark, not changed from pronunciation alone.
Ichigo means the whole span of life, equated with ikuru aida. The i, is an explanatory marker, not part of the Japanese phrase.

runs.text: Por toda vida, ou em quã

lines.note: Ichigo no aida is 'throughout one's life' or 'while one lives'. The Portuguese quã continues into quanto on the following row without a supplied hyphen.
To completes quanto, followed by viuer, 'to live'. The scan has i in viuer rather than OCR t; its historical u/v spelling is retained.

This ichigo is a berry, compared with amoras in the Portuguese gloss; no narrower botanical identification is imposed. The visible fruita corrects OCR fraita, while Morangãos remains the historical printed form.
Ichigoo is one hair, hitotsu no ke, then figuratively a tiny amount. The final hũ introduces tamanino on the next row, and the caron is retained.

Tamanino expresses the tiny-amount sense. Ichigoo midan no bonbu is the example of an ordinary person who has not cut away even a hair's breadth of faults; the dictionary supplies alternative Portuguese paraphrases below.

runs.text: Nem tamanho como hum cabelinho tenho de

lines.note: The first paraphrase denies possessing even a hair's breadth of virtue. The scan's tamanho and cabelinho are retained rather than made identical to the preceding diminutive tamanino.

runs.text: virtude, ou nem hũa minima falta poßo cortar

lines.note: The alternative paraphrase says the speaker cannot cut away even the smallest fault. Cortar is abraded at the right edge but remains readable with the following coordinated verb.
Afastar de mim completes the removal of a fault from oneself. The sentence closes the moral example attached to the tiny-amount sense of ichigoo.
Ichigoo here is one deed or work, hitotsu no waza. The circumflex distinguishes its printed form from the preceding hair term's caron.

runs.text: O eſtar inclinado a algũa arte,

lines.note: Ichigooshokan describes being deeply inclined toward a particular art or occupation. The following lines expand the explanation rather than supplying a second headword.

runs.text: ou modo de viuer que parece não auer outra

lines.note: The person's inclination is toward a way of life that seems to have no better alternative. The relative construction continues into couſa below.

runs.text: couſa na vida melhor pera ſe exercitar.

lines.note: The chosen occupation seems the best thing in life in which to exercise oneself. The worn close of exercitar is retained from the scan-supported word and construction.
Ichigoo shokanna mono illustrates a person of this inclination. The spacing between the two Japanese components is printed and is not normalized to the compound headword.

runs.text: ta maneira inclinado, ou afeiçoado a ſeu offi-

lines.note: Ta completes deſta. The person is inclined or attached to his occupation, with offi- divided across the row boundary.
Cio completes officio and closes the vocational-inclination example. The printed &c. is retained as the source's continuation marker.
Ichigon is one word or utterance. The short independent entry must not be merged with the preceding extended explanation.
Ichiguu is one meeting or encounter, paraphrased hitotsu voo. The diacritics are retained from this occurrence rather than inferred from other headwords.
This ichiguu is a corner, hitotsu no sumi. The examples begin with a house, ca- continued as caſa on the next line.
Sa completes caſa, followed by a figure or shape as another object with corners. This completes the geometrical or spatial sense.

runs.text: Hum eſquadrão que tem doze mil,

lines.note: Ichigun is defined as a military unit numbering twelve thousand plus the five hundred stated below. This records the dictionary's definition, not a claim about a modern unit's strength.
Five hundred soldiers completes the stated total of twelve thousand five hundred. The numeral belongs to the preceding ichigun definition.
Ichigwan is one wish or desire, hitotsu no negai. The gua sequence is the historical romanization and is not simplified.
Ichijaku is a determination, decision or settled resolution. The printed gi spelling is retained; the Portuguese aßento is not silently normalized.

runs.text: Hũa pintura, ou papel com algũa le

lines.note: Ichijiku denotes a hanging picture or inscribed sheet. Le continues into letra without a secure hyphen; the printed gi in the headword is kept rather than modernized to ji.
Tra completes letra, and the sheet is described as something hung up. Dependura is retained as the historical verb form in the print.
Ichijin is a grain or speck of dust, hitotsu no chiri. The scan includes the long s omitted in OCR pòinho, giving pòſinho; the alternative argueiro follows below.
Argueiro supplies another word for a speck. The figurative extension then means a very small amount, with ta- continued on the next line.
Manino completes tamanino, the tiny-amount gloss. The spelling is not replaced by a more familiar modern diminutive.
Ichijoo is a decision or determination, hitotsu no sadame. Determina continues into determinação, with no secure line-end hyphen added.
Ção completes determinação. The next sense is something certain or settled, with determina- divided from da below.
Da completes determinada. Ichijoo de gozaru is the example 'it is certain'; the printed particle remains joined to the preceding word.
Certa, & aueriguada completes the assertion that the matter is certain and established. The historical aueriguada is retained without modernization.
This ichijoo is a courtyard or open ground, distinct from determination. S marks written usage and is kept in the Portuguese italic span as supplied and supported by the scan.
Ichii is one heart or will, paraphrased hitotsu no kokoro. The scan has the internal hyphen in Ichi-i rather than OCR Ichiai; no unprinted full stop is supplied after it.
Ichii suru means uniting in will or becoming one body with someone. The scan reads em hum, not OCR emchum; corpo is a catchword here and the actual sentence continues on f260.
